dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product uses a hairline for ordinary boundaries and a heavier stroke for selection or emphasis.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Stroke widths for borders and dividers, multiples of dial.stroke.unit.

focus.$description: The focus indicator, from the control outwards: `offset` (negative = drawn inside the control), then an optional inner stroke in sys.color.focus-ring-inner, then the outer stroke in sys.color.focus-ring. Never animated.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product needs a focus indicator tuned apart from its borders: how far it sits from the control (or inside it, where an outer ring would be clipped), and optionally two tones so it stays visible on both light and dark areas of the same product.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Geometry of the keyboard focus indicator: outer and inner stroke widths and a signed offset (negative draws inside the control). Its colors are the roles focus-ring and focus-ring-inner.
rules: Every interactive component draws this indicator on keyboard focus only.
The indicator must keep 3:1 against what it is drawn on; the build checks it.

offset.$description: Distance from the control's edge to the indicator. Negative draws the indicator inside the control.

inner-width.$description: Width of the optional inner stroke. 0 = a single-tone ring.

target.$description: Minimum hit area. Visual size may be smaller; the hit area may not.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product is used by touch and by pointer, which need different minimum hit areas, and needs spacing between targets.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Minimum interactive target sizes (touch, pointer) and the spacing between targets. The hit area grows to these without changing how large a control looks.
rules: Never shrink a hit area below these to fit a layout.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows icons inside dense controls, in list rows and in navigation at different sizes, in one stroke weight, from one icon set, and tells a selected item from an unselected one by filling its icon — which a variable icon font does with an axis and a static one with a second family.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: How icons are drawn: the box sizes (extra-small 16, small 20, medium 24 — the default — and large 32), one weight for every icon and one for a control's own mark, and how a selected icon differs from an unselected one — by fill (a variable icon font) and/or by family (a static icon font). The default set is Material Symbols Rounded (ref.typeface.icon); its optical size follows the box size.
rules: An icon that represents something UNSELECTED uses family.unselected with fill.unselected (outlined); the same icon in its SELECTED state uses family.selected with fill.selected (filled). Always apply both — which of the two actually changes depends on the design system's icon set. Apply this consistently — navigation items, tabs, toggles, chips, favourites — and never mix filled and outlined icons for decoration.

Every icon uses sys.icon.weight, except a control's own mark (a checkbox's check and dash, the glyph on a switch's handle, the check in the box of a menu's checkbox item), which uses the weight its component token names; those alias sys.icon.mark.weight. Do not set an icon's or a mark's weight from a text style.

Components alias a size (a medium button → icon.medium); never write an icon size as a literal. medium is the standard glyph of a control, a row and a navigation destination; small and extra-small are for smaller or denser controls (a small button, a chip, a switch handle); large is for a large main action.

To change the icon set, a design system sets ref.typeface.icon (one variable font) or family.unselected / family.selected (a static set), and weight, and mark.weight. A static set has one weight: give both the same value. Icon NAMES are the product's concern: sets name their glyphs differently.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product draws a glyph inside a control that is itself dense — a switch handle, a small chip, a menu's check — smaller than the glyph it draws in a row or a button, and still from the same icon set.
One product has a main action drawn larger than its other controls — a large floating action button — whose glyph has to grow with it, or it reads as a small mark in a large shape.

weight.$description: The stroke weight of every icon (the `wght` axis of the icon font).

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: Material Symbols default weight in Material Design 3.

mark.$description: How a control's own mark is drawn where it differs from an icon: the check and the dash in a checkbox's box, the glyph on a switch's handle.

weight.$description: The stroke weight of a control's own mark (the `wght` axis of the icon font). A mark is a glyph of the same icon set as every icon, drawn at the small steps of the icon scale on a fill of the control; the default system draws it heavier than sys.icon.weight so that its stroke is wider than a pixel there.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product draws its icons in a light weight, which suits a 24 glyph beside a label, and finds the same weight too faint for the check in a checkbox or the glyph on a switch handle: those are 16 to 20 across, sit on a fill, and are what a person reads the control's state from. The weight of an icon and the weight of a control's mark are two decisions; a system whose icons are already heavy enough gives both the same value.

fill.$description: The fill of an icon by selection (the `FILL` axis of the icon font): 0 is outlined, 1 is filled.

unselected.$description: An icon for something that is not selected is outlined (FILL 0).

selected.$description: The same icon, selected, is filled (FILL 1).

optical-size.$description: The range of the icon font's optical-size axis (`opsz`), in the font's own units. A platform that sets the axis clamps the icon's box size into this range; it is a fact of the icon font the system names, not a design value.

min.$description: The smallest optical size the icon font draws (Material Symbols: 20).

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A property of the icon font, not of the design.

max.$description: The largest optical size the icon font draws (Material Symbols: 48).

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A property of the icon font, not of the design.

family.$description: The icon font by selection. A variable icon font (Material Symbols) is one family and tells selected from unselected with its FILL axis; a static icon font tells them apart with two families (Material Icons Outlined / Material Icons). Both default to ref.typeface.icon.

breakpoint.$description: The window widths at which a layout changes: the lower limit of each window class above compact. A window narrower than `medium` is compact. Widths of the window, never sizes of anything drawn.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product has one set of window classes: the width from which its navigation leaves the layout and the width from which there is room for a column beside the content are the same on every screen, whichever component asks.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: The two window widths that part compact, medium and expanded windows. A component that changes its layout with the window reads them through a component token of its own that aliases one of them.
rules: These are widths of the window, not of a container and not of anything drawn.
Never write a window width as a literal in a component; alias one of these.
Set both in a layer, or neither: medium is always below expanded.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A width of the window, not a size of anything drawn: no dial scales it.

medium.$description: The window width from which the class is medium. Below it the window is compact: one column, navigation over the content.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A width of the window, not a size of anything drawn: no dial scales it.

expanded.$description: The window width from which the class is expanded: there is room for navigation, and for a second column, beside the content.
